To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
palliative rehabilitation is an emerging field that has the potential to improve the lives of people with serious illnesses.
rehabilitation services are effective in the palliative care setting and that the integration of rehabilitation and palliative care is a promising area for future research.
rehabilitation interventions have been shown to be effective in improving function in patients with advanced cancer and that these interventions are underutilized.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: (1) the definition and scope of function‐directed treatment in palliative care; (2) the role of rehabilitation services in the palliative care continuum; (3) the evidence base for palliative rehabilitation; (4) the barriers to the delivery of rehabilitation services in palliation; and (5) the role of palliative rehabilitation in improving patient outcomes.
the following question: How can palliative care clinicians and rehabilitation professionals work together to optimize function and quality of life among advanced cancer patients?
the development of a palliative rehabilitation framework that is responsive to the needs of patients, families, and health care professionals and is consistent with the values of palliative care.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
palliative care and rehabilitation are complementary and synergistic.
the palliative rehabilitation is a multidisciplinary approach to rehabilitation of the patients with advanced cancer.

palliative rehabilitation is a function‐directed treatment delivered by a team of clinicians in the advanced cancer setting to address physical, emotional, and social needs and is aligned with the values and goals of the patient.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
rehabilitation is an essential element of palliative care, and palliative care is a critical element of rehabilitation.

palliative rehabilitation is a function‐directed approach to the management of advanced disease, and its implementation will be enhanced by greater understanding of its benefits and by greater attention to the challenges that impede its uptake.

the integration of palliative care and rehabilitation has the potential to improve the lives of patients and families facing life‐limiting illness, but the current lack of evidence‐based practice guidelines and a shared understanding of palliative rehabilitation will need to be addressed before this potential is realized.
The main takeaway from our work is that
rehabilitation services can be a powerful complement to palliative care and that the integration of functionally oriented care is feasible in a variety of settings.

the palliative care community has a responsibility to engage with rehabilitation services to ensure that patients' functional needs are addressed and to ensure that the palliative rehabilitation services that are available are of high quality and responsive to patients' needs.
rehabilitation is a vital part of palliative care, and that the two are not mutually exclusive.
